epics.title: Epidemiological Material Cataloging and Management
epics.jtbd: When the knowledge base administrator manages materials, I want to upload, categorize, and archive epidemiological protocols, so that the collection remains accurate and organized.
epics.sixSigmaMetric: Reduce average material cataloging processing time by 40%
requirements: R1: Administrator can upload document files (PDF, text) representing epidemiological protocols.
R2: Administrator can assign metadata (disease category, protocol type, publication date) to uploaded materials.
R3: Administrator can edit metadata of existing materials.
R4: Administrator can archive or delete outdated materials, with a confirmation prompt to prevent accidental data loss.
R5: The system provides explicit visible feedback upon successful upload or any validation failure.
R6: In case of submission failure, the user's entered metadata survives and is not cleared.
R7: Complex editorial approval workflows and automated stale-content detection are explicitly omitted as this is a direct cataloging utility for a trusted administrator team.

slices.title: Storage architecture decision for epidemiological materials
slices.jtbd: When implementing document storage for this epic, I want to decide between object storage and database BLOBs, so that the cataloging system is scalable and performant.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given the need to store large PDF protocols,
When evaluating object storage versus database BLOBs,
Then an ADR is drafted documenting the selected approach.
Given the ADR draft,
When reviewed by the team,
Then it is committed as a Markdown record in the repository.
slices.sixSigmaMetric: Zero ambiguity in storage implementation approach for subsequent tasks

epics.title: Epidemiological Material Search and Retrieval
epics.jtbd: When a health professional looks for guidance, I want to search and retrieve relevant epidemiological protocols, so that I can access accurate information during an outbreak.
epics.sixSigmaMetric: Reduce average time from search initiation to document retrieval to under 2 seconds
requirements: R1: Users can search for materials using keywords matching titles, descriptions, and assigned tags.
R2: Users can filter search results by disease category and specific protocol type.
R3: Users can view the detailed metadata and download or read the actual document.
R4: The system provides a clear empty-state message and recovery suggestions if a search yields zero results.
R5: The system provides explicit error feedback if a document fails to load or download due to network issues.
R6: Offline access to previously viewed documents is explicitly omitted as the system assumes an active network connection for the web portal.

epics.title: Knowledge Base Utilization Measurement
epics.jtbd: Goal: Ensure epidemiologists can efficiently find needed protocols. Questions: 1) Are searches resulting in document retrievals? 2) How quickly are documents found? 3) Which searches yield no results? When evaluating the knowledge base's impact, I want to measure these metrics via search success and retrieval times, so that the knowledge base's usefulness is demonstrably tracked.
epics.sixSigmaMetric: Increase the percentage of successful searches (leading to a document view) to >90%
requirements: R1: Goal: Ensure epidemiologists can efficiently find needed protocols.
R2: Question 1: Are searches resulting in document retrievals? Answered by tracking the percentage of searches that result in zero clicks or zero results.
R3: Question 2: How quickly are documents found? Answered by tracking the time taken from search initiation to document opening.
R4: Question 3: Which searches yield no results? Answered by logging query strings that result in zero-click or zero-result events to identify critical content gaps.
R5: These metrics must be recorded in the database and be programmatically accessible via a basic reporting endpoint.

slices.sixSigmaMetric: Achieve 100% test coverage for the metrics tracking endpoints and logic

epics.title: Disaster Recovery and Data Continuity
epics.jtbd: When managing a system containing critical epidemiological records whose loss would harm the operation, I want to ensure automated backups run and recovery is proven, so that data availability is guaranteed during an incident.
epics.sixSigmaMetric: 100% of catastrophic data loss scenarios can be successfully reverted within the agreed recovery time objective
requirements: R1: The system must perform regular, automated backups of the document storage and relational database.
R2: The backup restoration process must be formally documented, actively performed, and verified against a staging environment to prove viability.

slices.title: Configuration of automated backups
slices.jtbd: When implementing infrastructure for this epic, I want to configure the automated backup jobs, so that database and document assets are safely archived.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given the production infrastructure,
When the backup cron executes,
Then a complete snapshot of database and object storage is saved to a secure secondary location.
Given a failed backup job,
When detected,
Then an alert is immediately raised to the infrastructure team.

slices.title: Verification of complete data restoration
slices.jtbd: When verifying disaster recovery for this epic, I want to execute a full restore from a backup artifact into an isolated environment, so that the backups are proven to be viable.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a recent backup artifact,
When the restore procedure is executed in a staging environment,
Then the database and document storage are completely recovered without data corruption.
Given the restored environment,
When validation tests run,
Then critical application workflows function exactly as they did before the snapshot.
slices.sixSigmaMetric: Recovery Time Objective (RTO) achieved during the validation exercise

epics.title: Baseline Epidemiological Content Provisioning
epics.jtbd: When demonstrating the system to the buyer, I want the database pre-loaded with real epidemiological protocols, so that all search and cataloging workflows can be visually verified.
epics.sixSigmaMetric: 100% of functional acceptance criteria can be verified using the pre-loaded real data
requirements: R1: The system must be initialized with at least 10 real-world epidemiological protocols (e.g., standard WHO guidelines for COVID-19, Cholera, Measles).
R2: The initialized materials must contain comprehensive, realistic metadata, including tags and disease categories, to fully exercise the search filters.
